kid.simple: Gives the text of the key the player should press for a KeyCode, matching their keyboard layout. For example on a French keyboard, `KeyCode.Q` gives "A" because the keys are in different places.
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
print("Press " .. UserInputService:GetStringForKeyCode(Enum.KeyCode.E) .. " to open")

m.d:
This method returns an array of KeyCodes that the gamepad associated with the given UserInputType supports. If called on a non‑connected gamepad, returns an empty array.

To determine if a specific KeyCode is supported, use GamepadSupports().
m.s: Returns an array of `Enum.KeyCode|KeyCodes` that the gamepad associated with the given `Enum.UserInputType` supports.

p.s: The UserInputType of the gamepad.

r.s: An array of KeyCodes supported by the given gamepad.

kid.simple: Lists every button (KeyCode) a controller has. Empty if that controller is not connected.
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
for _, code in UserInputService:GetSupportedGamepadKeyCodes(Enum.UserInputType.Gamepad1) do
    print(code.Name)
end

m.d:
The UserInputService:GetUserCFrame() method returns a CFrame describing the position and orientation of a specified UserCFrame virtual reality (VR) device. If the specified device is not connected, the method returns CFrame.new().

For example, the code snippet below prints the CFrame of the user's VR headset.

local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
local cframe = UserInputService:GetUserCFrame(Enum.UserCFrame.Head)

print(cframe)

By using the method, players can implement features such as re-positioning the user's in-game character corresponding to the location of a connected VR device. This can be done by changing the CFrame of the user's in-game body parts to match the CFrame of the specified VR device using UserCFrame and CFrame value arguments passed by the event.

See also:

  • UserInputService.UserCFrameChanged, an event which fires when the CFrame of a VR device changes
  • VRService, a service used to implement VR support

As this event only fires locally, it can only be used in a LocalScript.
m.s: Returns a `Datatype.CFrame` describing the position and orientation of a specified virtual reality device.

p.s: The UserCFrame corresponding to the VR device.

r.s: A CFrame describing the position and orientation of the specified VR device.

kid.simple: Old — use `VRService:GetUserCFrame()` instead.

m.d:
This method returns true if a particular button is pressed on a gamepad, otherwise returns false.

See also InputBinding as a way to hook gamepad and other input interactions to InputActions.
m.s: Determines whether a particular button is pressed on a gamepad.

p.s: The UserInputType of the given gamepad.
The KeyCode of the specified gamepad button.

r.s: Whether the specified button on the given gamepad is pressed is pressed.

kid.simple: True if a certain button on a certain controller is held down right now.
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
if UserInputService:IsGamepadButtonDown(Enum.UserInputType.Gamepad1, Enum.KeyCode.ButtonA) then
    print("A is held")
end

m.d:
This method returns true if a particular key is pressed on a keyboard, otherwise returns false.

See also InputBinding as a way to hook key and other input interactions to InputActions.
m.s: Returns whether the given `Enum.KeyCode|key` is currently held down.

p.s: The KeyCode of the key.

r.s: Whether the specified key is being held down.

kid.simple: True if a certain keyboard key is held down right now. Great for checking keys inside a frame loop.
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
RunService.PreRender:Connect(function()
    if UserInputService:IsKeyDown(Enum.KeyCode.Space) then
        print("Space is held")
    end
end)

m.d:
This method returns true if a particular mouse button is pressed, otherwise returns false.

See also InputBinding as a way to hook mouse button and other input interactions to InputActions.
m.s: Returns whether the given mouse button is currently held down.

p.s: The UserInputType of the mouse button.

r.s: Whether the given mouse button is currently held down.

kid.simple: True if a certain mouse button is held down right now. Use `Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1` for left, `MouseButton2` for right.
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
print(UserInputService:IsMouseButtonPressed(Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1))

m.d:
This method returns true if the specified gamepad is allowed to control navigation and selection GuiObjects.

Use SetNavigationGamepad() to set a navigation gamepad, or GetNavigationGamepads() to get a list of all navigation gamepads.
m.s: Returns `true` if the specified gamepad is allowed to control navigation and selection `Class.GuiObject|GuiObjects`.

p.s: The UserInputType of the specified gamepad.

r.s: Whether the specified gamepad is a navigation gamepad.

kid.simple: True if a controller is allowed to move the selection around menus.
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
print(UserInputService:IsNavigationGamepad(Enum.UserInputType.Gamepad1))

m.d:
This method recenters the CFrame of the VR headset to the current orientation of the headset worn by the user. This means that the headset's current orientation is set to CFrame.new().

This method behaves identically to the VRService method RecenterUserHeadCFrame().
m.s: Recenters the `Datatype.CFrame` of the VR headset to the current orientation of the headset worn by the user.

kid.simple: For VR headsets: makes the way the player is facing right now count as "straight ahead". Same as `VRService:RecenterUserHeadCFrame()`.
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
UserInputService:RecenterUserHeadCFrame()

m.d:
This method sets whether the specified gamepad can move the GuiObject navigator.

Use IsNavigationGamepad() to check if a specified gamepad is a set to be a navigation gamepad, or GetNavigationGamepads() to retrieve a list of all navigation gamepads.
m.s: Sets whether or not the specified gamepad can move the `Class.GuiObject` navigator.

p.s: The UserInputType of the specified gamepad.
Whether the specified gamepad can move the GUI navigator.

kid.simple: Turns on or off whether a controller can move the selection around menus.
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
UserInputService:SetNavigationGamepad(Enum.UserInputType.Gamepad1, true)

m.d:
This event fires when a user moves a device that has an accelerometer, a component found in most mobile devices that measures acceleration (change in speed). To determine whether a user's device has an accelerometer enabled, use AccelerometerEnabled.

This event can be used along with GetDeviceAcceleration() to determine the current movement of a user's device.
m.s: Fires when a user moves a device that has an accelerometer.

p.s: An InputObject, with a UserInputType of Accelerometer and Position that shows the force of gravity on each local device axis.

kid.simple: Fires when a phone with an accelerometer is moved or shaken. Gives an InputObject; its `Position` has the acceleration numbers.
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
UserInputService.DeviceAccelerationChanged:Connect(function(acceleration)
    if acceleration.Position.Magnitude > 2 then -- Magnitude = total strength
        print("You shook the phone!")
    end
end)

m.d:
This event fires when the device's gravity Vector3 changes on a device that has an accelerometer. To determine whether a user's device has an accelerometer enabled, use AccelerometerEnabled.

A device's gravity vector represent the force of gravity on each of the device's X, Y, and Z axes. While gravity never changes, the force it exerts on each axis changes when the device rotates and changes orientation. The force value exerted on each axis is a unit vector ranging from -1 to 1.

If the device has an enabled accelerometer, you can use the GetDeviceGravity() method to get the current force of gravity on the user's device.
m.s: Fires when the force of gravity changes on a device that has an enabled accelerometer.

p.s: An InputObject with a Position property that shows the force of gravity on each local device axis. This position can be used as a direction to determine the direction of gravity relative to the device.

kid.simple: Fires when the pull of gravity changes direction compared to the phone, which happens when the phone is tilted. Gives an InputObject whose `Position` shows the gravity direction.
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
UserInputService.DeviceGravityChanged:Connect(function(gravity)
    print("Tilt:", gravity.Position)
end)

m.d:
This event fires when a user rotates a device that has a gyroscope, a component found in most mobile devices that detects orientation and rotational speed. To check if a user's device has an enabled gyroscope, use GyroscopeEnabled.

To query the current device rotation, use the GetDeviceRotation() method.

Note that this event only fires when the Roblox client window is in focus. Inputs will not be captured when the window is minimized.
m.s: Fires when a user rotates a device that has a gyroscope.

p.s: An InputObject providing info about the device's rotation. Position represents the new rotation a Vector3 positional value and Delta represents the change in rotation in a Vector3 positional value.
A CFrame representing the device's current orientation.

kid.simple: Fires when a device with a gyroscope is turned. Gives an InputObject and a CFrame describing the new rotation.
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
UserInputService.DeviceRotationChanged:Connect(function(rotation, cframe)
    print("Device turned:", cframe)
end)

m.d:
This event fires when a gamepad is connected to the client. You can also use GetConnectedGamepads() to find the correct gamepad to use.

Alternatively, you can detect value changes to the PreferredInput property which more accurately reflects which input (mouse/keyboard, touch, gamepad, etc.) the player is likely using as the primary input.

See also GamepadDisconnected.
m.s: Fires when a gamepad is connected to the client.

p.s: The UserInputType of the connected gamepad.

kid.simple: Fires when a controller is plugged in. Tells you which one (like `Gamepad1`).
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
UserInputService.GamepadConnected:Connect(function(gamepad)
    print(gamepad.Name, "connected")
end)

m.d:
This event fires when a gamepad is disconnected from the client.

Alternatively, you can detect value changes to the PreferredInput property which more accurately reflects which input (mouse/keyboard, touch, gamepad, etc.) the player is likely using as the primary input.

See also GamepadConnected.
m.s: Fires when a gamepad is disconnected from the client.

p.s: TheUserInputType of the disconnected gamepad.

kid.simple: Fires when a controller is unplugged. Tells you which one.
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
UserInputService.GamepadDisconnected:Connect(function(gamepad)
    print(gamepad.Name, "disconnected")
end)

m.d:
This event fires when a user begins interacting with an input device such as a mouse or gamepad, such as when they first interact with a gamepad button, although it does not capture mouse wheel movements. Can be used along with InputChanged and InputEnded to track when user input begins, changes, and ends.

See also InputBinding as a way to hook input device interactions to InputActions.

Note that this event only fires when the Roblox client window is in focus. It will not fire when the window is minimized.
m.s: Fires when a user begins interacting with an input device such as a mouse or gamepad.

p.s: An InputObject instance containing information about the user's input.

Indicates whether the engine internally observed this input and acted on it. Generally this refers to UI processing, so if a button was touched or clicked from this input, gameProcessedEvent will be true.

kid.simple: Fires when the player STARTS an input: presses a key, clicks, touches the screen or presses a controller button. Gives the InputObject and gameProcessedEvent (true if Roblox already used it, like chat typing). Does not catch the mouse wheel.
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, gameProcessedEvent)
    if gameProcessedEvent then return end
    if input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.F then
        print("F pressed")
    end
end)
kid.gotcha: Forgetting the gameProcessedEvent check means typing in chat triggers your controls.

m.d:
This event fires when a user changes how they're interacting with an input device such as a mouse or gamepad. Can be used along with InputBegan and InputEnded to track when user input begins, changes, and ends.

See also InputBinding as a way to hook input device interactions to InputActions.

Note that this event only fires when the Roblox client window is in focus. It will not fire when the window is minimized.
m.s: Fires when a user changes how they're interacting with an input device such as a mouse or gamepad.

p.s: An InputObject instance containing information about the user's input.

Indicates whether the engine internally observed this input and acted on it. Generally this refers to UI processing, so if a button was touched or clicked from this input, gameProcessedEvent will be true. To ignore events that are automatically handled by Roblox like scrolling in a ScrollingFrame, check that gameProcessedEvent is false.

kid.simple: Fires when an input CHANGES while happening: the mouse moves, the mouse wheel scrolls, a joystick tilts, or a finger slides.
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
UserInputService.InputChanged:Connect(function(input, gameProcessedEvent)
    if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseWheel then
        print("Scrolled:", input.Position.Z) -- 1 = up, -1 = down
    end
end)

m.d:
This event fires when a user stops interacting with an input device such as a mouse or gamepad, such as when they release a gamepad button. Can be used along with InputBegan and InputChanged to track when user input begins, changes, and ends.

See also InputBinding as a way to hook input device interactions to InputActions.

Note that this event only fires when the Roblox client window is in focus. It will not fire when the window is minimized.
m.s: Fires when a user stops interacting with an input device such as a mouse or gamepad.

p.s: An InputObject instance containing information about the user input.

Indicates whether the engine internally observed this input and acted on it. Generally this refers to UI processing, so if a button was touched or clicked from this input, gameProcessedEvent will be true.

kid.simple: Fires when the player STOPS an input: lets go of a key or button, or lifts a finger.
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
UserInputService.InputEnded:Connect(function(input, gameProcessedEvent)
    if input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.F then
        print("F released")
    end
end)

m.d:
This event fires when there is a jump request from the client, for example when the client presses the spacebar or jump button on mobile. Default behavior is to set the player's Humanoid.Jump property to true which makes the player's character jump.

Since this event fires multiple times for a single jump request, using a debounce is recommended. This event does not fire if Player.Character is set to nil.
m.s: Fires whenever the client makes a request for their character to jump.

kid.simple: Fires when the player tries to jump (Space, the jump button on phones, or A on a controller).
kid.example:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
local lastJump = 0
UserInputService.JumpRequest:Connect(function()
    if os.clock() - lastJump > 0.5 then -- debounce: only once every half second
        lastJump = os.clock()

end)

m.d:
The UserCFrameChanged event fires when the CFrame of a VR device changes.

This event can be used to track the movement of a connected VR device.

Using the event, you can implement features such as moving the user's in-game character limbs as the user moves their VR device. This can be done by changing the CFrame of the user's in-game limbs to match the CFrame changes of the VR device using the UserCFrame enum and CFrame value arguments passed by the event.

To retrieve the CFrame of a connected VR device, use UserInputService:GetUserCFrame().

As the event fires locally, it can only be used in a LocalScript.

See also:

  • VRService, used to implement support, including an identical event VRService.UserHeadCFrameChanged
  • Camera.HeadLocked, when this property is true the Camera will automatically track the head motion of a player using a VR device
  • Camera:GetRenderCFrame(), a method which retrieves the CFrame the Camera is being orientated at, including the impact of VR devices
m.s: Fires when the `Datatype.CFrame` of a specified Virtual Reality device changes.

p.s: A UserCFrame value indicating which body part moved.
A CFrame value indicating the updated CFrame of the body part that moved.

    print("Player tabbed out")

kid.simple: UserInputService tells your game what the player is pressing, clicking, tapping or tilting. It can tell you when a key goes down or up, where the mouse is, if a finger touches the screen, and what kind of device the player has (keyboard, gamepad, touch screen). It only works in code that runs on the player's own device.
kid.analogy: UserInputService is like a security guard watching every button on the player's keyboard, mouse, controller and screen. Whenever something is pressed, released or moved, the guard radios your script and tells it exactly what happened.
whenToUse: Do something when the player presses a key, like E to open a door or Shift to sprint
Check if a key is being held down right now
Find where the mouse is on the screen, or lock it in the middle for a first-person game
React to taps, swipes and pinches on phones and tablets
Find out if the player is using a keyboard, gamepad or touch screen so you can show the right buttons
kid.where: Client only. Use it in a LocalScript (for example in StarterPlayerScripts or StarterCharacterScripts) with game:GetService("UserInputService"). It does not work in server Scripts, because the server has no keyboard.

terms.input: Anything the player does with a device: pressing a key, clicking, moving the mouse, touching the screen, pushing a joystick.
terms.InputObject: A little package of information about one input. It has `KeyCode` (which key or button), `UserInputType` (keyboard, mouse, touch, gamepad...), `UserInputState` (began, changed, ended) and `Position`.
terms.KeyCode: The name of a key or button, like `Enum.KeyCode.E`, `Enum.KeyCode.Space` or `Enum.KeyCode.ButtonA` on a gamepad.
terms.UserInputType: What kind of input it was, like `Enum.UserInputType.Keyboard`, `MouseButton1` (left click), `Touch` or `Gamepad1`.
terms.gameProcessedEvent: True if Roblox already used this input for something else, like typing in the chat box or clicking a GUI button. Usually you should ignore those inputs so pressing E while chatting does not open a door.
terms.client: The player's own device (computer, phone, console). LocalScripts run here.
terms.server: Roblox's computer that runs the game for everyone. It cannot see a player's keyboard.
terms.gamepad: A game controller, like an Xbox or PlayStation controller.
terms.accelerometer: A sensor in phones that feels how fast the phone is speeding up or shaking.
terms.gyroscope: A sensor in phones that feels how the phone is turning or tilting.
terms.focus: Which thing is currently "selected" to receive typing. A TextBox has focus when you click it to type. The game window has focus when it is the window in front.
terms.pixels: The tiny dots that make up your screen. Screen positions are measured in pixels from the top-left corner (0, 0).
terms.Vector2: Two numbers together, X (left-right) and Y (up-down), used for screen positions.
terms.debounce: A simple on/off check that stops code from running many times in a row too quickly.
terms.event: A signal that something happened. You `:Connect` a function to it and it runs each time.
terms.deprecated: Old. Still there so old games do not break, but you should use the newer thing instead.

examples.title: Press E to say hello
examples.code:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, gameProcessedEvent)
    -- if the player was typing in chat (or clicking a button), ignore it
    if gameProcessedEvent then
        return
    end

    if input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.E then
        print("You pressed E!")
    elseif input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 then
        print("You clicked the left mouse button")
    end
end)
explain: `InputBegan` fires the moment any key, button or touch starts.
`input` tells us what it was. `gameProcessedEvent` is true if Roblox already used it, for example the player was typing in the chat.
We check `input.KeyCode` for keys, and `input.UserInputType` for mouse buttons.

examples.title: Hold Shift to sprint
examples.code:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

local humanoid = script.Parent:WaitForChild("Humanoid")

local NORMAL_SPEED = 16
local SPRINT_SPEED = 28

UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, gameProcessedEvent)
    if gameProcessedEvent then return end
    if input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift then
        humanoid.WalkSpeed = SPRINT_SPEED -- key went down: run
    end
end)

UserInputService.InputEnded:Connect(function(input, gameProcessedEvent)
    if input.KeyCode == Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift then
        humanoid.WalkSpeed = NORMAL_SPEED -- key came up: walk
    end
end)
explain: A LocalScript in StarterCharacterScripts is placed inside the character, so `script.Parent` is the character.
`InputBegan` fires when Shift goes down, `InputEnded` when it comes back up.
Changing WalkSpeed from the player's own device works for their own character's movement.

examples.title: Show the right hint for the player's device
examples.code:
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

local function showHint()
    local preferred = UserInputService.PreferredInput
    if preferred == Enum.PreferredInput.Touch then
        print("Tap the button to jump")
    elseif preferred == Enum.PreferredInput.Gamepad then
        print("Press A to jump")
    else
        print("Press Space to jump")
    end
end

showHint()
-- update the hint if the player switches, e.g. picks up a controller
UserInputService:GetPropertyChangedSignal("PreferredInput"):Connect(showHint)
explain: `PreferredInput` is Roblox's best guess at what the player is mainly using right now.
We show a hint that matches it, and listen for changes so the hint updates when they switch devices.

gotchas: It only works on the client. Putting this code in a server Script does nothing useful. Use a LocalScript.
Always check `gameProcessedEvent`. Otherwise typing "e" in chat will also trigger your E-key action.
Key presses only change things for that player. To change something for everyone (give coins, open a shared door), send a RemoteEvent to the server.
`InputBegan` does not catch mouse wheel scrolling; use `InputChanged` for that.
To lock the mouse with `MouseBehavior`, you may need to set it again every frame, because the default camera scripts can change it back.
Many touch and window events only fire while the Roblox window is in focus (in front).

class/UserService.d: A service that handles queries regarding users on the Roblox platform.
class/UserService.s: A service that handles queries regarding users on the Roblox platform.

m.d:
This function lets you request information about users outside of the current DataModel in bulk. The input and output values are both arrays.

  • The order of the user info objects in the return value's array may not match the order of the UserIds sent in the input parameter's array. Use the Id field of the user info object to identify your input array with the output array.
  • It's possible to receive fewer user info objects than requested if one or more of the UserIds in the request array are invalid, such as negative numbers or user IDs that don't have accounts associated with them. It's possible to receive a response with zero results if all UserIds are invalid.
  • If a Roblox user does not have a DisplayName associated with their account, this function will instead return the same string as the user's username in their info object's DisplayName field. While a user's UserId will never change, they may change their username or display name, so the same input UserIds may return a different string for these fields from one day to another.
  • Since GetUserInfosByUserIdsAsync() makes an external web request, it will yield and may fail if the backend service is experiencing interruptions. Ensure you can handle downtime appropriately by wrapping this method with a LuaGlobals.pcall().
  • Results are limited to 250 per minute, so if you receive an HTTP 429 error, try again later, ideally after reducing the number of UserIds in your input array, reducing the number of method calls, or both.

The signature of a singular user info object is:

Key Type Description
Id number The Class.Player.UserId|UserId associated with the user.
Username string The username associated with the user.
DisplayName string The Class.Player.DisplayName|DisplayName associated with the user.
HasVerifiedBadge boolean The Class.Player.HasVerifiedBadge|HasVerifiedBadge value associated with the user.
m.s: Returns an array of user information including user name and display name.

p.s: An array of UserIds requested.

r.s: An array of dictionary objects that contain user information.
